export type User = {
  id: string;
  email: string;
  name: string;
  createdAt: string;
};

const users: User[] = [
  { id: "1", email: "ada@example.com", name: "Ada", createdAt: "2026-01-04" },
  { id: "2", email: "grace@example.com", name: "Grace", createdAt: "2026-02-11" },
];

export async function listUsers(): Promise<User[]> {
  return users;
}

export async function getUser(id: string): Promise<User | undefined> {
  return users.find((u) => u.id === id);
}

// TODO: there is no real session handling yet — the dashboard just picks the first user.
export async function getCurrentUser(): Promise<User | undefined> {
  return users[0];
}

content.text:
I added a 10-minute reminder job using Inngest. `next build` passes and eslint is clean, but I haven't run the job end to end, so the 10-minute delay and the retries are untested.

- **Library:** Inngest. It handles the delay and retries itself, so you don't need Redis or a worker process. It runs as a Next.js route.
- **`src/lib/users.ts`:** there was no way to create a user, so I added `createUser({ email, name })`. It adds the user and sends a `notely/user.created` event. If the queue is unreachable it logs the error and still returns the user.
- **`src/inngest/functions.ts`:** the `user-reminder` job waits 10 minutes, then logs a reminder. It makes up to 5 attempts (`retries: 4`) with exponential backoff.
- **`src/inngest/client.ts` and `src/app/api/inngest/route.ts`:** the Inngest client and the endpoint Inngest calls to run jobs.
- **`.env.example`:** placeholder `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY` and `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY`, plus an optional `INNGEST_DEV=1` for local use. `.gitignore` ignored every `.env*` file, so I added an exception for `.env.example`.

Nothing calls `createUser` yet, because the app has no signup route or form.

To try it locally, set `INNGEST_DEV=1`, run `npx inngest-cli@latest dev` alongside `npm run dev`, and call `createUser`. In production, put real keys from app.inngest.com in the environment and register `/api/inngest` with Inngest.

`tsc --noEmit` reports an error in `src/app/layout.tsx` (`LayoutProps` not found). It was already there before my changes, and `next build` type-checks fine.
